rationale: Recharge and water-table level are shared across a catchment or aquifer: the benefit is not confined to the adopting farm.
Carbon removal is a global public good: no farm-level beneficiary.
Biodiversity gains accrue at landscape scale (habitat and connectivity) beyond the plot.
Bunds; terraces; dams and spate works cut runoff peaks downstream of the works; the flood-damage evidence is downstream.
In-field and terrace practices hold soil on the adopter's own plot.
Harvested water and soil moisture serve the adopter's own crops.
Food-security gains are measured in the adopting households.
Income and returns are measured in the adopting households.
Buffers attenuate flood peaks and bank erosion downstream along the channel.
The buffer holds the field edge (on-farm) and traps sediment that would reach the stream (downstream).
Storm-surge and flood protection lands on the coast behind the stand.
Fishery and aquaculture income can accrue to households working the stand; protection value lands behind it.
